content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots are cooked carrot pieces packed in glass or metal jars with added fat (usually vegetable oil) to enhance flavor and preserve texture. The product is ready to eat straight from the jar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning extends the shelf life of carrots up to 2‑3 years.
The added fat helps retain aromatic compounds, giving a richer taste.
Carrots are one of the most popular vegetables for canning because of their natural sweetness.
In many countries canned carrots are a staple ingredient in salads like Olivier and Russian salad.
Traditional cans often contain olive or sunflower oil.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision and immunity.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B6 and B2 are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: The added vegetable oil enhances the bioavailability of vitamin A and other carotenoids.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The product can be calorie‑dense; those watching weight should consider portion size.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may react to the oil used in the can.

items.title: Bacterial safety
items.content: A damaged jar can allow bacterial growth, so always check the integrity of the packaging.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, stews, used in snacks and sandwiches, or lightly warmed in the microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the carrots in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 5‑7 days.
